# Canonical normalization of a zero-endpoint critical circuit

This lemma explains how the canonical cap coordinates in the companion
three-fiber theorems arise from a general actual ambient configuration.
It is a lattice-preserving normalization, not an assertion that every
mixed-depth maximizer has the required circuit.

Let d>=1. Let A,K,B be full-dimensional fibers at integer bases -1,0,1,
with (A+B)/2 subset K. Let y lie in int K. Suppose d+1 ambient closed
halfspaces through (0,y), written as

    u_i.x+beta_i z>=u_i.y,

attain the source's genuine raw depth, each has a proper A cut and
zero B-volume, and the nonzero continuous normals u_i form a full-rank
minimal positive circuit. Then an invertible continuous affine map and
fiber shear, leaving z unchanged, send this configuration to

    source (0,0),
    H_i={(z,x'):v_i.x'>=z},
    B' subset T_0={x':v_i.x'<=1},
    sum_i v_i=0,

where T_0 can be any fixed centroid-zero simplex, with a corresponding
permutation of the facets. In particular one can take v_1,...,v_d to
be the coordinate covectors and v_(d+1)=-(v_1+...+v_d).

## Proof

Put h_i=h_B(u_i). The B threshold of the i-th cap is u_i.y-beta_i.
Its zero volume implies this threshold is at least h_i. If it were
strictly greater, move it slightly toward B while preserving the
continuous normal and the middle threshold. The B cap remains empty;
the proper A threshold moves inward and its captured volume strictly
decreases. This contradicts genuine ambient criticality. Therefore

    beta_i=u_i.y-h_i.

The cap family is exactly

    u_i.x+(u_i.y-h_i)z>=u_i.y.                     (1)

The support polytope

    T={x:u_i.x<=h_i for every i}

is a bounded full-dimensional simplex. It has interior because it
contains B. Boundedness follows from the full-rank positive circuit:
a recession direction r would satisfy u_i.r<=0 for every i, and the
positive dependence then forces all equalities, hence r=0. With d+1
facet normals in minimal dependence, no inequality is redundant and
the resulting bounded full-dimensional polytope is a simplex.

Let g be the centroid of T and put a_i=h_i-u_i.g>0. The normalized
normals u_i/a_i sum to zero. Here is a direct verification retaining
the precise factors. If P_i is the vertex opposite the i-th facet,
then every P_j with j!=i satisfies u_i.P_j=h_i. Since

g=(P_1+...+P_(d+1))/(d+1),

    h_i-u_i.P_i=(d+1)a_i.

Thus the affine functions

    lambda_i(x)=(h_i-u_i.x)/[(d+1)a_i]

have the Kronecker vertex values of the barycentric coordinates of T.
Their sum is identically one, so the sum of their linear parts is zero.
This proves sum_i u_i/a_i=0.

Choose an invertible linear map L carrying T-g to the desired
centroid-zero simplex T_0, with matched facet labels. Define

    v_i=u_i L^(-1)/a_i,
    (z,x) -> (z,x')=(z,L[x-y-z(g-y)]).             (2)

At the source this sends y to0. On the B fiber it sends T to T_0,
since x'=L(x-g) when z=1. On the A and K fibers it gives

    A'=L(A+g-2y),
    K'=L(K-y),
    B'=L(B-g).

Consequently (A'+B')/2 subset K'. Substitution of the inverse map
into (1) gives

    u_i L^(-1)x'+z(u_i.g-h_i)>=0,
    v_i.x'>=z,

as asserted. The sum of the v_i is zero by the preceding calculation.

The entire map (2) is invertible affine, leaves the integer coordinate
exactly unchanged, and is a bijection of Z times R^d. It maps ambient
closed halfspaces bijectively to ambient closed halfspaces. On every
full-dimensional continuous fiber it multiplies ordinary volume by the
same constant |det L|. Hence normalized mixed depths and criticality
are preserved, while raw mixed depths acquire that common factor.
Properness of the A cuts, zero B-volume, convexity, and actual midpoint
compatibility are all preserved. No full-ambient normal balance or
centroid condition on y has been assumed. QED.

## Scope

This normalization applies to the stated full-dimensional three-fiber
configuration and its full-rank continuous positive circuit. It does
not prove the existence of that circuit in a general OC instance, and
it does not claim a common volume factor for arbitrary lower-dimensional
Hausdorff fibers outside these hypotheses.
